title: Forgotten forests
authors: Michael Gross
abstract: The ongoing loss of the Amazonian rainforest is a key environmental concern highlighted by the recent COP30 meeting in Belém and on many other occasions. However, many other forests from the Arctic Circle to southern Chile are also threatened by human activities and climate change.

title: Nokwanda Makunga
authors: Nokwanda Makunga
abstract: Interview with Nokwanda (Nox) Makunga, who uses biotechnology to study the genetics and metabolism of medicinal plants at Stellenbosch University.

title: Ballistic tongues
authors: Yu Zeng, Stephen M. Deban
abstract: Zeng and Deban provide an overview of ballistic tongues in three vertebrates, highlighting similarities and differences in launch and retraction mechanisms, ecological advantages, evolutionary history, and open questions.

title: Cognitive maps
authors: Yossi Yovel
abstract: Yossi Yovel summarizes the concept of the cognitive map, its definition, history, current research, neural basis and non-spatial equivalents.

title: Ecology: Mycorrhizas within the entangled bank on the most remote island on Earth
authors: Susana Rodríguez Echeverría
abstract: A new study mapping the diversity of mycorrhizal fungi on the Palmyra Atoll shows their role as key links between land and sea. The fungi support the health of trees where seabirds nest; in turn, the seabirds deliver nutrients that fuel both terrestrial and marine systems.

authors: Luke R. Thompson
abstract: A long-standing tenet of microbiology is that Earth’s microbiomes are structured by environment, not geography. authors: Ansgar Büschges, E. Axel Gorostiza
abstract: Targeted leg grooming in insects relies on a continuous somatotopic representation that spans all processing stages, from sensory bristle projections to motor neuron output. abstract: New work reveals that elephant whiskers, also known as vibrissae, have elliptical, stiff, and porous bases along with soft tips. title: Biological timing: The dark side of light around the clock
authors: Anne C. Skeldon, Derk-Jan Dijk
abstract: Regular 24-hour light–dark cycles are essential for biological time-keeping and the temporal organisation of our brains and bodies. authors: Anna Karnkowska, Ivan García-Cunchillos
abstract: Emblematic animals of coral reefs, corals and giant clams, host intra- and extracellular dinoflagellate symbionts, respectively. title: Neuroscience: Shared circuits for care
authors: Wing Gee Shum, Johannes Kohl
abstract: Prosocial behaviors — actions that benefit others — may build on neural systems originally evolved for parental care, but direct evidence has been scarce. A new study in mice reveals partially overlapping circuits that mediate care for pups and distressed adult conspecifics.

authors: Kyle E. Miller
abstract: Body motion bends and stretches axons. title: Multinucleation as a recurring evolutionary strategy for scaling and plasticity
authors: Gautam Dey, Markus Ganter, Marie Jacobovitz
abstract: Here, Dey, Ganter, and Jacobovitz integrate perspectives from cell biology, ecology, and evolution to demonstrate that multinucleation is not a rare anomaly but a fundamental organizational strategy for addressing issues of scale, coordination, and adaptability to environmental constraints.
